title: The Second Chebyshev Function: From θ to ψ
content: The module docstring explains ψ(n) as the natural extension of θ(n): where θ sums log p over primes p ≤ n, ψ sums log p over all prime powers p^j ≤ n. Since von Mangoldt Λ(p) = log p and Λ(p^j) = log p for all j ≥ 1, the definition ψ(n) = Σ_{k ≤ n} Λ(k) neatly unifies both. The difference ψ(n) - θ(n) counts contributions from prime squares, cubes, etc. — only O(√n · log n) total, so asymptotically negligible. The key results listed (θ ≤ ψ, upper bound ψ ≤ 2n·log 2, Bertrand lower bound, PNT equivalence) build from most concrete to most profound.
mathContext: $\psi(n) = \sum_{k=1}^n \Lambda(k) = \sum_{p^j \leq n} \log p$ where $\Lambda(k) = \log p$ if $k = p^j$ for some prime $p$ and $j \geq 1$, else $\Lambda(k) = 0$. The excess $\psi(n) - \theta(n) = \sum_{p^j \leq n,\, j \geq 2} \log p = O(\sqrt{n} \log n)$.

title: Definitions of ψ and θ Using Mathlib's vonMangoldt
content: Both Chebyshev functions are defined as Finset sums over ranges. `chebyshevPsi n` sums Mathlib's `vonMangoldt k` over k ∈ range(n+1), matching the classical ψ(n) = Σ_{k ≤ n} Λ(k). `chebyshevThetaOQ n` restricts to primes in range(n+1) and sums Real.log p, giving θ(n) = Σ_{p prime, p ≤ n} log p. Both are proved non-negative: ψ via `vonMangoldt_nonneg`, and θ via `Real.log_nonneg` using p ≥ 2 for primes. The key identity `vonMangoldt_prime_eq` applies Mathlib's `vonMangoldt_apply_prime` to confirm Λ(p) = log p for primes — the bridge between the two definitions.
mathContext: \text{chebyshevPsi}(n) = \sum_{k \in \text{range}(n+1)} \Lambda(k), \quad \text{chebyshevThetaOQ}(n) = \sum_{\substack{p \in \text{range}(n+1) \\ p \text{ prime}}} \log p. \quad \Lambda(k) \geq 0 \text{ always, and } \Lambda(p) = \log p \text{ for prime } p.

title: θ(n) ≤ ψ(n): Subset Sum Monotonicity via vonMangoldt
content: The proof of θ(n) ≤ ψ(n) uses a two-step strategy. First, `chebyshevThetaOQ_eq_sumVonMangoldt` rewrites θ(n) by replacing log p with vonMangoldt p for each prime p, using `Finset.sum_congr` with `vonMangoldt_apply_prime`. This converts the θ sum from 'log p over primes' to 'vonMangoldt over primes'. Second, `theta_le_psi_via_vonMangoldt` applies `Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg`: since filter Nat.Prime (range n+1) ⊆ range (n+1), and vonMangoldt ≥ 0, the sum over the prime subset ≤ the sum over all of range(n+1). Chaining these two steps yields θ ≤ ψ.
mathContext: \theta(n) = \sum_{p \leq n,\, p \text{ prime}} \log p = \sum_{p \leq n,\, p \text{ prime}} \Lambda(p) \leq \sum_{k \leq n} \Lambda(k) = \psi(n). \text{ The inequality holds since } \Lambda(k) \geq 0 \text{ and the prime filter is a subset.}

title: Upper Bound ψ(n) ≤ 2n·log 2 via Central Binomial Coefficients
content: The two axioms here capture the Chebyshev upper bound. `chebyshevPsi_doubling_le` axiomatizes ψ(2n) - ψ(n) ≤ 2n·log 2: the classical proof observes that any prime power p^j in (n, 2n] divides C(2n, n) (the central binomial), and C(2n, n) ≤ 4^n = 2^{2n}, so the product of all such prime powers is ≤ 4^n, giving ψ(2n) - ψ(n) ≤ log(4^n) = 2n·log 2. The full bound `chebyshevPsi_upper_bound` follows by the telescoping argument ψ(n) = Σ_{k} [ψ(n/2^k) - ψ(n/2^{k+1})] ≤ Σ_k (n/2^k)·log 2 ≤ 2n·log 2. Both are axiomatized because the Lean formalization of the binomial coefficient argument requires careful work.

title: Lower Bound via Bertrand's Postulate: ψ(2n) - ψ(n) ≥ log(n+1)
content: This is the most substantial proved (non-axiom) result in the file. The proof uses Bertrand's postulate (`Nat.exists_prime_lt_and_le_two_mul_add_one`) to obtain a prime p with n < p ≤ 2n. Since p > n, we have log p ≥ log(n+1). The key step shows p contributes vonMangoldt p = log p to ψ(2n) but not to ψ(n), so the difference is at least log p ≥ log(n+1). The Lean tactic proof uses `Finset.sum_sdiff` and `Finset.single_le_sum` to extract p's contribution from the set-difference (range(2n+1) \ range(n+1)). The calc block chains: log(n+1) ≤ log p = Λ(p) ≤ ψ(2n) - ψ(n).
mathContext: \text{Bertrand: } \exists p \text{ prime, } n < p \leq 2n. \text{ Then } \log(n+1) \leq \log p = \Lambda(p) \leq \psi(2n) - \psi(n) \text{ since } p \in [1,2n] \setminus [1,n].

title: The Prime Number Theorem as an Axiom: ψ(n)/n → 1
content: These two axioms capture the deepest results. `chebyshevPsi_asymptotic` asserts ψ(n)/n → 1 in Filter.atTop as a Lean Filter.Tendsto statement — this is the Prime Number Theorem (PNT) in its ψ-form. `pnt_equivalence` states the classical equivalence between this and the more familiar π(n) ~ n/log n form. Both are axiomatized because the full PNT proof requires either complex analysis of the Riemann zeta function (Hadamard-de la Vallée Poussin 1896) or the elementary but highly technical Selberg-Erdős proof (1949). Lean formalizations of PNT exist but are not yet in Mathlib main.
mathContext: \frac{\psi(n)}{n} \to 1 \iff \pi(n) \sim \frac{n}{\log n}. \text{ Both forms follow from showing } \zeta(s) \text{ has no zeros on } \Re(s)=1 \text{ (PNT criterion)}. \text{ Equivalence proved via Abel summation.}

title: Summary Theorem: Sandwich of ψ(n) Between θ(n) and 2n·log 2
content: The final theorem `chebyshevPsi_bounds` packages the two proved results: θ(n) ≤ ψ(n) (from the vonMangoldt subset argument) and the Bertrand lower bound ψ(n) ≥ log(n/2 + 1). The lower bound is obtained by applying `chebyshevPsi_doubling_lower` to n/2 and using non-negativity of ψ(n/2). Combined with the axiomatized upper bound, this gives the Chebyshev sandwich: log(n/2 + 1) ≤ ψ(n) ≤ 2n·log 2. Asymptotically, both bounds are Θ(n), consistent with ψ(n) ~ n (PNT). The proof uses linarith to close the lower bound from the Bertrand lemma.
mathContext: \log\!\left(\tfrac{n}{2}+1\right) \leq \psi(n) \leq 2n \log 2, \quad \theta(n) \leq \psi(n). \text{ Chebyshev (1852) proved } \frac{5}{6} n \leq \psi(n) \leq \frac{12}{10} n \text{ (improving the constants); PNT gives } \psi(n) \sim n.
